FROM   TPCDS_DB.store_sales ss
LEFT JOIN TPCDS_DB.promotion p ON ss.ss_promo_sk = p.p_promo_sk AND p.p_channel_tv = 'N'
WHERE  ss.ss_customer_sk IS NULL

diagnosis.bottleneck: The query spends most time scanning and filtering store_sales (node 1) for ss_customer_sk IS NULL; the left table after filtering is still large enough to dominate runtime, while the broadcast join (node 8) and aggregations (nodes 10, 12) are trivial because the right side (promotion) is only ~300 rows.

plan_nodes.note: LeftOuter BuildRight; Left keys [1]: [ss_promo_sk#51339]; Right keys [1]: [p_promo_sk#51354]; Join type: LeftOuter; Join

hypotheses.claim: A filter on the joined side sits in the ON clause of a LEFT JOIN; the join dominates the cost. (matched: left join tpcds_db.promotion p on … and p.p_channel_tv = ')
The IsNull(ss_customer_sk) predicate is not selective enough, causing a near-full scan of the store_sales fact table; adding a partition filter or indexing on ss_customer_sk would reduce I/O.

The left outer broadcast join forces a hash lookup for every qualifying store_sales row even though the build side is tiny; converting to an inner join (if semantically valid) or pre-aggregating the left side before the join could cut CPU.

The single-partition exchange between the two hash aggregates (nodes 10 → 12) serializes the final reduction; since the result is just two scalars, a local aggregation on the driver after collecting partials would avoid the shuffle.
